meta.topic: Critical UAT failure rate at test start

problem:
Beacon Bank is starting user acceptance testing for a new SEPA direct debit collection service. On the first morning, the failure rate is critical: most test collections are rejected, mandate references cannot be found, and the test schedule shows collections submitted on the wrong day. The test manager wants to push on and log defects as they come. The business analyst suspects the problem is not the software but the readiness of the test itself: the environment, the test data, the build and the requirements may each be wrong in a different way, and continuing to test against a broken setup will produce defect noise that hides the real faults.

The learner must triage before deciding whether to continue, pause or stop. That means checking the environment configuration, the mandate test data, the build version, and whether the requirements the testers are using match the current scheme rules. The scheme facts matter here: an SDD Core collection must be submitted by D-1, one Inter-PSP Business Day before the Due Date, with pre-notification at the latest 14 Calendar Days before the Due Date, and an unused mandate must not be used after 36 months. A test that submits on the wrong day or uses a stale mandate will fail for the right reasons, and logging those as software defects wastes the whole test window. The case tests the discipline of an entry gate: UAT starts only when its entry criteria are met.
solution:
Begin with a triage that separates the failure causes into four buckets: environment, test data, build and requirements. Check the environment first: is the UAT build the intended version, are the endpoints, credentials and scheme adapters pointed at the right test systems, and are the feature flags set as the release notes state? Then check the test data: do the mandate references exist in the test system, are the mandates within their validity, has any mandate been unused for 36 months, and are the collection dates consistent with the D-1 submission deadline and the 14-calendar-day pre-notification rule? Then check the requirements the testers are using against the current scheme rules, and confirm the test cases match them.

Segment the failures by bucket and count them, so the decision rests on numbers rather than impressions. If the cause is environment or data, fix the readiness gap, re-run the entry criteria and restart the affected test cases with a clean record. If the cause is the build, raise defects with reproducible evidence and ask the test manager to decide whether the remaining test scope is still meaningful. If the requirements themselves are wrong, stop and correct them before any more testing. Record the triage, the entry criteria results and the continue, pause or stop decision, and re-plan the test window with the time the fix actually needs rather than the time the schedule wishes for.

decision.question: Beacon Bank starts UAT for a new SEPA direct debit collection service. On the first morning most test collections fail: mandate references cannot be found and collections are submitted on the wrong day. The test manager wants to push on. You are the business analyst asked to triage before deciding whether to continue.

options.label: A
options.detail: Declare the build unfit and cancel UAT without checking the environment or the data.

options.label: B
options.detail: Push on with testing and log every failure as a software defect, since UAT is about finding defects.

options.label: C
options.detail: Change the test data to make the tests pass, since the schedule is tight.

options.label: D
options.detail: Pause and triage environment, test data, build and requirements against entry criteria, then decide to continue, pause or stop with evidence.

decisionRationale: Option D is correct because a critical failure rate at test start usually signals a readiness failure, and testing against a broken setup produces noise, not evidence. Option B logs environment and data failures as software defects. Option A blames the build without evidence. Option C falsifies the test and destroys its value.

steps.title: Halt new test execution and open the triage record
Segment failures by environment, data, build and requirements
Verify build version, endpoints, credentials and feature flags
Verify mandate references, validity and collection dates against scheme rules
Check test cases against current SDD rules and requirements
Decide continue, pause or stop and re-plan the test window
Record the decision and the entry criteria evidence

happy: UAT restarts only after the entry criteria pass: the right build is deployed, the mandate data is valid and consistent with the D-1 and pre-notification rules, and the test cases match the current requirements. Failures found after restart are genuine defects with reproducible evidence, and the test plan reflects the time the fix actually needed.

negative.title: Mandate reference not found
negative.detail: Test data references mandates that were never loaded into the UAT environment. Reload the mandate data, verify each reference exists, and re-run the affected cases with a clean record.

negative.title: Collection submitted on the wrong day
negative.detail: Test cases use a submission date that breaches the D-1 deadline. Correct the test schedule to the scheme rule and treat the earlier failures as data errors, not software defects.

negative.title: Stale mandate used in testing
negative.detail: A mandate unused for 36 months is used in a test case. Remove the mandate from the test data, since an unused mandate must not be used after 36 months, and replace it with a valid one.

negative.title: Environment points at the wrong downstream
negative.detail: UAT calls a test adapter that returns production-shaped errors. Correct the endpoint and configuration, verify the build version, and re-run the entry criteria before restarting.

technical: Keep the entry criteria checklist with a pass or fail per item, the build version, the environment configuration and the test data inventory versioned together so a failure can be reproduced. Log every defect with the test case, the data used, the build version and the environment, so a defect can be separated from a readiness failure. Store the triage segmentation with counts per bucket, and keep the requirements traceability matrix current so a test case can be traced to the scheme rule it checks.

accounting: A failed UAT collection in the test environment has no real financial effect, but the operational lesson is financial: if the same readiness failure reached production, collections would be rejected, creditors would miss expected funds, and returns and refunds would follow under scheme rules. Core returns run to D+5 Inter-PSP Business Days and B2B returns to D+3, authorised Core refunds run within 8 weeks of the debit date with no questions asked, and unauthorised claims run within 13 months. Operations must be able to explain to a creditor why a collection was rejected, which rule it breached, and what must change before resubmission, so the UAT defect record should capture the business meaning of each failure, not only its technical symptom.

scenarios.then: failures are segmented by environment, data, build and requirements before any continue decision is made.

scenarios.then: the test data is corrected because the mandate must not be used.

questions.question: What is the SDD Core collection submission deadline?
options: D-1, one Inter-PSP Business Day before the Due Date
questions.explanation: The SDD Core collection submission deadline is D-1, one Inter-PSP Business Day before the Due Date, not D-2.

questions.question: How long before the Due Date must pre-notification be sent at the latest?
questions.explanation: Pre-notification must be sent at the latest 14 Calendar Days before the Due Date.

questions.question: Why should testing pause when the failure rate is critical at the start of UAT?
options: Because the build is always at fault
Because the failures may come from environment or data readiness, and testing on will produce defect noise that hides real faults
questions.explanation: A critical early failure rate usually signals a readiness failure, and continuing produces noise rather than evidence.

questions.question: What happens to a mandate unused for 36 months?
options: It needs a new creditor ID
questions.explanation: A mandate unused for 36 months must not be used.
